title: Multi-Tenant B2B Event Analytics Engine
problem: Software-as-a-service telemetry systems collect high-volume behavioral event streams from web and mobile applications, but executing ad-hoc funnel conversions and cohort retention aggregations on row-oriented transactional databases creates severe disk I/O bottlenecks and query timeouts. Relational databases store records contiguously on disk, forcing full-row deserialization even when queries touch only a few analytical columns. A multi-tenant analytics platform overcomes this limitation by streaming telemetry through an ingestion buffer into a columnar storage engine, compressing column payloads with dictionary and delta encodings and leveraging partitioned sparse primary keys to achieve sub-second analytical aggregations across multi-tenant datasets.
use_cases: Multi-step conversion funnel analysis across tenant user onboarding workflows
Weekly and monthly retention cohort calculation for subscription software products
Real-time event frequency monitoring and anomaly inspection across organizational workspaces
hard_parts: Preventing ClickHouse part explosion errors triggered by unbuffered high-frequency event ingestion
Structuring sparse primary keys to balance tenant-level isolation with temporal range scan performance
Managing deduplication consistency in ReplacingMergeTree tables without incurring severe query-time merge overhead
Formulating vectorized SQL queries using windowFunnel and retention functions within bounded server memory limits
screener_signals: Reproducible Docker environment launching ClickHouse, Kafka, and ingestion services with automated health checks
Validated benchmark suite demonstrating batch insert throughput and sub-100ms funnel query latencies
Anti-fake verification script validating dynamic tenant isolation and live columnar mutations

components.name: Beacon Ingestion Receiver
components.purpose: Validates incoming telemetry payloads against strict schemas and publishes to partitioned Kafka topics

components.name: Buffer Ingestion Pipeline
components.purpose: Consumes stream data pipelines and flushes micro-batches into ClickHouse columnar databases

components.name: Columnar Analytical Storage
components.purpose: Stores event rows in a ReplacingMergeTree table sorted by tenant_id, event_name, and timestamp with ZSTD compression

components.name: Multi-Tenant Query Service
components.purpose: Exposes parameterized analytical APIs executing windowFunnel and retention cohort SQL aggregations

components.name: Containerized Test Environment
components.purpose: Orchestrates isolated local execution of ClickHouse, Kafka broker, and Node.js microservices

architecture.data_flow: Client HTTP beacons are ingested by Node.js; validated events are buffered in Kafka topics partitioned by tenant; consumer groups aggregate records into micro-batches of several thousand rows; batches are inserted into ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree tables; analytical dashboard queries invoke specialized ClickHouse SQL functions to compute aggregate funnels and cohorts.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Ingestion service enforces batch flush boundaries (either batch threshold or maximum time interval) to prevent part explosion; ClickHouse table schema enforces primary index sorting on tenant_id and timestamp.

targets.method: Synthetic streaming harness benchmarking sustained row insertions per second into ClickHouse
targets.input: 100,000 synthetic JSON event beacons flushed in micro-batches of 5,000 rows
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, 8GB RAM, Docker ClickHouse 23+
targets.minimum_pass: Sustained ingestion throughput > 5,000 events/sec without part errors
targets.target: Sustained ingestion throughput > 12,000 events/sec without part errors
targets.report: Benchmark execution summary log reporting duration and throughput metrics

targets.method: Autocannon load test executing windowFunnel SQL aggregation across tenant clickstream data
targets.input: 500,000 historical event rows across 5 active tenant workspaces
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Docker ClickHouse 23+, query cache disabled
targets.minimum_pass: p95 query latency < 120ms across 50 concurrent requests
targets.target: p95 query latency < 65ms across 50 concurrent requests
targets.report: Autocannon latency distribution output and ClickHouse system.query_log extract

targets.method: Inspection of uncompressed data bytes versus compressed bytes stored on disk via system.parts
targets.input: 500,000 ingested events containing string identifiers and JSON payload attributes
targets.environment: Standard local Docker volume on ext4/NTFS/APFS filesystem
targets.minimum_pass: Compression ratio >= 4.0:1 on event storage columns
targets.target: Compression ratio >= 6.5:1 on event storage columns
targets.report: SQL report output querying data_compressed_bytes and data_uncompressed_bytes in system.parts

starter_input.spec: Deterministic synthetic telemetry generator producing event beacons with tenant UUID, user UUID, session ID, event name, timestamp, and properties.
starter_input.size: 500,000 synthetic event records distributed across 5 tenant workspaces and 20,000 simulated user accounts
starter_input.seeded_cases: Funnel drop-off points, out-of-order event timestamps within a 15-minute window, duplicate event IDs, and high-frequency click bursts
starter_input.label_source: Deterministic JavaScript event generation script using fixed seed 1337
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly synthetic user identifiers and mock events; no personal data or live tracking cookies used

prerequisites: Basic SQL aggregation principles (GROUP BY, JOIN, aggregate window functions)
Familiarity with Docker and container networking

environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Engine 24+ and Node.js 18+ installed
environment.fallback_path: Standalone single-binary ClickHouse local server without Kafka using an in-memory Node.js buffer queue

riskiest_component.name: ClickHouse Part Explosion During High-Frequency Event Ingestion
riskiest_component.fallback: Application-level in-memory ring buffer enforcing strict 5,000-event batch flushes or 2-second timeout intervals with disk fallback

worksheet.q1: The student builds a multi-tenant event analytics engine that buffers event beacons in Kafka, batch-loads them into ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree tables, and exposes APIs for fast conversion funnel and cohort retention aggregations.
worksheet.q2: Core path: single-node ClickHouse with optimized primary keys, Node.js batch ingestion buffer, analytical API with windowFunnel, and 500k event benchmark. Extended path: multi-node distributed ClickHouse cluster with ZooKeeper replication and AggregatingMergeTree materialized views (+14h).
worksheet.q3: Components: ClickHouse Schema (5h), Kafka & Batch Buffer (4h), TypeScript Ingestion HTTP (4h), Analytical SQL Queries (4h), Synthetic Generator & Benchmark (4h), Docs & Buffer (4h). Subtotal 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: Data analysis/BI, Data pipeline/ETL/streaming. Metrics built: Batch Ingestion Write Throughput, Funnel Query Latency, Columnar Disk Compression Ratio. Rejected: real-time streaming lag under multi-datacenter network partitions (out of scope for core OLAP analytics).
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: part explosion from unbuffered inserts, primary index key order tradeoffs, ReplacingMergeTree deduplication overhead, and memory limits during windowFunnel executions.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: synthetic clickstream telemetry generator producing 500,000 event records across 5 tenants with fixed seed 1337; seeded edge cases include funnel drop-offs, out-of-order timestamps, and duplicate event IDs. No real personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local single-binary ClickHouse CLI without Kafka.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: ClickHouse part explosion during high-frequency ingestion. Fallback: application-level ring buffer flushing every 5,000 items or 2s.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded JSON funnel metrics. Anti-fake rubric item 5 creates a dynamic tenant ID with randomized events at runtime and verifies live database state mutation.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Not required; strictly synthetic telemetry data.
